## Natural history notes

A small aquatic crambid moth characterized by pale tan to whitish wings sprinkled with fine brown speckling, giving it a “dewy” or lightly dusted appearance. In Florida, the Dewy Leafcutter is recorded from the state and is most likely found around ponds, lakes, sluggish streams, canals, marshes, and other still or slow-moving waters with aquatic vegetation. The larvae are aquatic; their exact host plants appear undocumented, but they are suspected to feed on algae or submerged plant material, while adults may come to lights near wetlands and serve as prey for bats, spiders, and other insect predators.
